frames.narration: A fetcher asks the frontier for work. The frontier looks for a site that is not being rested. news.example was last fetched 3 seconds ago and its gap is 2, so it hands over its next URL.
The fetcher needs the server's address and the site's rules. Both are already in the cache, so there is no DNS lookup and no robots.txt download.
The fetcher downloads the page with a timeout and a size limit. The frontier now marks news.example as resting for the next 2 seconds.
The raw page is saved in the page store, keyed by its URL. If the worker crashes and fetches it again, the same key is simply overwritten.
The parser finds 31 links. Each is cleaned up: lower-case host, fragment removed, trailing slash tidied. HTTP://News.Example:80/story/43#c becomes http://news.example/story/43.
Each cleaned URL is checked against the seen set. 27 are known already and are dropped. Four are new and are recorded.

The new URLs go into the queues of their own sites. Three belong to news.example and wait their turn behind the rest of its queue. One belongs to another site and will be picked up at once by a free worker.
Later the scheduler will put story/42 back in the frontier. A news page that changed since last time is revisited within hours, while a page that has not changed in a year is revisited in weeks.
